name: CityFee – City Dropdown & Delivery Fees for WooCommerce
author: Mohamed Salem KHATTAT

sections.description:
In many countries couriers price delivery by city, not by postcode, and customers type their city in many different ways. CityFee replaces the free-text city field with a dropdown (a select list) of the cities you deliver to and charges the delivery fee of the chosen city: city-wise delivery charges that you set. It is built for Cash on Delivery stores, but works for any WooCommerce store that ships by city.

Free features

  • City dropdown at checkout instead of a free-text city field, per country, in the classic checkout and the Checkout block, for billing and shipping addresses.
  • The customer can only pick a city from your list, and the choice is checked on the server too.
  • Your own city lists: add, edit, hide and reorder cities in WooCommerce > CityFee. An optional “other spelling” (for example the name in Arabic script) is shown next to the name.
  • Paste a whole list at once: one city per line, optionally with its fee. You can copy two columns (city and fee) from a spreadsheet and paste them directly.
  • “Delivery by city” shipping method: a fee per city, a default fee for cities without one, and “not delivered” cities that get no delivery option.
  • The fee updates as soon as the customer changes the city.
  • Change many fees at once (bulk edit for selected cities or a whole country).
  • Cities can also be used as regions in WooCommerce shipping zones.
  • The chosen city is copied into the order and customer address, so emails, invoices and courier exports show a normal city name.
  • Postcode field hidden per country (optional).
  • Compatible with HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage).
  • Translation-ready and right-to-left ready (admin screen and checkout checked in Arabic).

How it works

  1. Go to WooCommerce > CityFee, choose a country and add or paste your cities with their fees.
  2. In WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping, add “Delivery by city” to the shipping zone that covers the country, like Flat rate, and set the default fee.
  3. Customers now choose their city from the list and see its delivery fee at checkout.

CityFee comes without city lists: you add your own, so the list matches your courier’s cities exactly. Try it first with “Load demo cities” (7 cities of Mauritania).

CityFee Pro

A paid version, CityFee Pro, adds city groups (for example Zone A / B / C) with one fee per group, free delivery above a cart amount per city or group, hiding Cash on Delivery for selected cities, and full CSV import and export of your city lists. The free plugin works on its own and shows no advertising.

Pricing and a 7-day free trial (no card needed): dssarl.com/cityfee

Privacy

CityFee does not send any data to external services and adds no tracking. City lists and settings are stored in your WordPress database; orders and customer addresses use WooCommerce’s normal fields.

CityFee is developed by Digital Services SARL (https://dssarl.com/).

Getting fake Cash on Delivery orders? Our free plugin OrderProof asks customers to confirm COD orders with a WhatsApp code before you ship.

Questions or problems? Open a thread in the support forum. If CityFee is useful to your store, an honest review helps other store owners find it.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install CityFee from Plugins > Add New, or upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/, and activate it.
  3. Open WooCommerce > CityFee to add your first country and its cities.
  4. Add the “Delivery by city” method to a shipping zone in WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping.
sections.faq:
How do I add my cities and fees quickly?

Go to WooCommerce > CityFee, choose the country and paste one city per line. Add the fee after a semicolon:

Casablanca;30
Rabat;35
Tanger

Cities without a fee use the default fee of “Delivery by city”. Fees are plain numbers in the store currency. Two columns copied from a spreadsheet (city, fee) work the same way. Tick “Check only” to count the lines before saving anything.

Can I set different delivery charges for each city?

Yes. Each city can have its own fee, cities without a fee use the default fee of “Delivery by city”, and you can change many fees at once with bulk edit.

Does it work for my country?

Yes. Choose any country in WooCommerce > CityFee and add the cities your courier serves. You can show another spelling next to each name, for example in Arabic script. If WooCommerce asks for a region (state) in your country, the city list takes its place (see below).

Does it work with the Checkout block?

Yes. The city dropdown and the fee work in both the classic checkout and the Checkout block.

Does it come with city lists?

Not yet. You add or paste your own list, so it matches your courier’s cities exactly.

What happens to the country’s region (state) field?

For a country where you turn the city dropdown on, the city list takes the place of the region field. Stores that need both a region and a city should keep that country switched off.

What if I don’t deliver to a city?

Mark it “Not delivered”. It stays in the list, but “Delivery by city” offers no rate for it, so WooCommerce shows its usual “no shipping options” message unless another method of the zone (for example local pickup) is available.

Can I rename a city later?

Yes. Each city has a code that orders store; renaming the city keeps its code. Past orders keep the address they were placed with.

How many cities can a country have?

Up to 2,000. Above 300 the admin shows a reminder, because the Checkout block shows a plain dropdown without search.

Is it translated?

CityFee is ready for translation and for right-to-left languages. French and Arabic translations have been prepared for translate.wordpress.org.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

The city lists, the CityFee settings and the “Delivery by city” methods in your shipping zones. Orders and customer addresses are never changed. Tick “Keep city lists and settings when the plugin is deleted” if you plan to reinstall.
sections.changelog:
1.0.1

  • Readme: clearer short description and description, two new FAQ entries (fees per city, supported countries), support forum link, screenshot 2 caption. No change to how the plugin works.

1.0.0

  • First public release: city dropdown per country in the classic checkout and the Checkout block (billing and shipping), server-side city check, city lists managed in WooCommerce > CityFee (add, edit, hide, reorder, bulk fee changes, paste-import with fees), “Delivery by city” shipping method (fee per city, default fee, not-delivered cities, tax status), cities usable as regions in shipping zones, city copied into orders and customer addresses, optional postcode hiding, HPOS compatible, translation and right-to-left ready, uninstall cleanup with a “keep data” option.

short_description: City dropdown at checkout and shipping fees by city, for Cash on Delivery stores where couriers price by city. Classic and block checkout.
